source: NCERT Class XII, Introductory Macroeconomics, Ch. 3 (Money and Banking).

sections.heading: 1. Money — Functions and Forms
points: **Money** solves the problem of **barter** (double coincidence of wants).

sub: **Medium of exchange, unit of account (measure of value), store of value, and standard of deferred payment.**

points: Forms: **fiat money** (legal by government order, e.g. notes/coins), **fiduciary money** (accepted on trust, e.g. cheques), and **legal tender**.

sections.heading: 2. Money Supply — Measures
points: **Money supply** = total money held by the public at a point in time.

sub: **M1** = currency with public + demand deposits + other deposits with RBI (narrow money).
**M2** = M1 + savings deposits with post office.
**M3** = M1 + time (fixed) deposits with banks (broad money — most used).

sections.heading: 3. Banks and Credit Creation
points: **Commercial banks** accept deposits and give loans; they **create credit (money)** by lending out a multiple of their reserves.
**Money multiplier** = 1 ÷ reserve ratio; banks keep only a fraction (reserves) and lend the rest.
Demand deposits are the main part of money created by banks.

sections.heading: 4. The Central Bank (RBI) and Monetary Policy
points: The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the central bank: **issues currency, banker to the government and banks, controls credit, manages foreign exchange**.
It is the **'lender of last resort'**.

sub: **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** — reserve requirements.
**Repo rate** (RBI lends to banks) and **Reverse repo rate**; **Bank Rate**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Functions of money: medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value, deferred payment.
M1 = narrow money; M3 = broad money (most used).
Banks create credit; money multiplier = 1 ÷ reserve ratio.
RBI = central bank, lender of last resort, issues currency.
Monetary tools: CRR, SLR, repo/reverse repo rate, OMO.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **M1 = narrow money; M3 = broad money** (M3 = M1 + time deposits).
**CRR = cash reserve with RBI; SLR = liquid assets** banks must keep.
The **repo rate** is the rate at which **RBI lends to banks**.
The RBI is the **'lender of last resort'** and issues currency.
